status: in progress; overall throughput and memory parity not achieved
acceptance: Keep pursuing throughput and memory parity before accepting the pivot.
implementation: One Arc-owned WebTransport Session is shared by the application task and output sink. Only shared async/immutable methods are used; per-clone poll state is not used. The larger, cold HTTP3 admission future is boxed outside the spawned task and released when the handshake completes. Its result is already Arc-owned, keeping the full Session out of the persistent frame. The connection-count lease is captured before spawning, so cancellation before first poll also releases ownership. Framing, transport parameters, queue limits, delivery, observer ordering, routing, crypto and congestion control are unchanged.
tradeoffs: One persistent Arc allocation and a transient admission-future allocation per physical connection replace copied Session handles/metadata and larger task frames. No per-message allocation was introduced. HTTP3 async APIs retain their own waiter registrations.
scope: Local Linux loopback; ordinary release builds, frozen verifying clients, sequential benchmark processes. Three alternating fresh-process throughput runs per case/variant. Four pinned server workers on CPUs 0-3, eight pinned client workers on CPUs 8-15, four seconds, 1 KiB payloads, 32 private pairs, 1024 room readers, fanout window four. Capacity uses eight server workers on CPUs 0-7, 100000 physical QUIC connections, four offered seconds and 400000 exactly verified deliveries. Latency percentiles are logarithmic upper bounds. RSS is sampled at gates and excludes kernel socket memory; it is neither continuous peak nor requested live heap.

capacity_order.wrapper_note: capacity.run returns None after writing the successful authoritative receipt; initial wrapper incorrectly subscripted it. No child failure. Corrected for subsequent invocations.

historical_controls.scope: Earlier measured controls, not rerun during this checkpoint. Plaintext is the existing acceptance baseline. TLS control includes both proxy and backend CPU/RSS and an extra loopback hop; it is not native-WSS performance or a general protocol ceiling.

freshness_scope: One final candidate check per clean/loss/reorder mode. 360 offered 1 KiB states at 60 Hz over six seconds plus reliable 1 MiB bulk. Loss profile: 20 ms one-way and 2% packet loss; reorder additionally 8 ms jitter and 25% reordering. External port only, both directions, temporary isolated namespace; TLS proxy internal hop unimpaired. Same seeds/parameters are not identical packet-loss trajectories. Probes include initial state before first update; stale sequences cannot replace new state. Unreceived updates are not attributed exclusively to network loss. Single samples do not establish statistical protocol rankings.
remaining: Overall parity remains unmet: memory and room/mixed throughput remain behind the plaintext control, mixed private traffic remains behind the earlier encrypted fixture. Continue active QUIC connection/HTTP3 storage and reliable scheduling work. Observer cancellation/re-subscribe, full concurrent 100k/8192 inspection, broader overload/shutdown, QUIC buffer accounting, final packaging and deployment documentation remain required. No acceptance, push, release or deployment claim.
